countingUnit: Conservatively grouped established inference/forecast mechanism, not a configuration or complete executable trading system.
noveltyAuditLimit: Not located in inspected current source and research artifacts; this is not a proof of absence from all git history, hidden files or external literature.

methods.name: Hidden Markov model of recurring return regimes
equations: z_t | z_(t-1)=i ~ Categorical(A_i); r_t | z_t=j ~ g_j(r_t; theta_j).
alpha_t(j) proportional_to g_j(r_t) * sum_i A_ij * alpha_(t-1)(i).
p(r_(t+1) | r_(1:t)) = sum_ij alpha_t(i) * A_ij * g_j(r_(t+1)).
methods.mechanismNovelty: A latent state persists probabilistically and can recur. The inspected regime model is a supervised feature-split tree; it has no hidden-state transition law or forward probability recursion.
requiredObservations: Completed daily returns, optionally completed volume or spread proxies with their availability timestamps.
Contiguous training and later sequential forecast blocks; enough regime transitions for any meaningful assessment.
methods.economicHypothesis: If return dynamics recur in persistent regimes, conditioning on filtered regime uncertainty could avoid applying one unconditional relationship across incompatible conditions. Whether conditional means exceed fees remains unknown.

primarySources.title: Rabiner, A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition (1989)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Do not count state numbers, emission distributions, labels bull/bear or symbol choices as new mechanisms.
A threshold trend label or CART leaf renamed a hidden state does not qualify.
Filtered inference is required at each decision; smoothing using future observations leaks information.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: 720 daily bars support a small research implementation, not reliable profitability or stable regime-parameter estimates.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Predeclare two latent regimes and a causal training/forecast schedule; score next-observation predictive density before any funded net-return replay.

methods.frozenSpecification: Three Gaussian states; first 90 returns only; 40 regularized EM updates; 14-day expected log growth; fixed base-cost hurdle; ETH long or cash.

methods.name: Bayesian online changepoint detection with posterior run length
equations: Predictive distribution = sum_l p(l_t=l | r_(1:t)) * p(r_(t+1) | current_segment_l).
methods.mechanismNovelty: Maintains probability over the age of the current data-generating segment and marginalizes segment forecasts. Existing CUSUM accumulates threshold evidence; existing DynamicBayes exponentially decays all sufficient statistics. Neither represents a posterior over structural-reset locations.
requiredObservations: Ordered completed daily returns and exact observation availability.
Segment-prior and hazard declarations made before outcomes; no retrospectively chosen change dates.
methods.economicHypothesis: If abrupt changes make old data actively misleading, a run-length posterior could adapt faster than fixed forgetting while retaining uncertainty about whether a change occurred. More resets can also overreact to ordinary noise.

primarySources.title: Adams and MacKay, Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (2007)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Changing CUSUM thresholds or an EWMA half-life is excluded.
Different hazard rates or conjugate priors are configurations of this one mechanism.
Unlike F01, segments have newly drawn parameters rather than membership in a fixed set of recurring latent states.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Sample supports run-length inference and predictive diagnostics; rare changes and reused dates limit generalization.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Freeze one hazard/prior before replay; compare sequential log scores against fixed-forgetting Bayesian estimates on the same observations.

methods.name: Nonlinear Gaussian-process predictive regression
methods.mechanismNovelty: Uses a joint function prior and predictive covariance over training/query locations. Existing kernel estimation computes recency-weighted local empirical outcome averages; existing ridge uses a finite fixed linear map.
requiredObservations: Causal feature vectors and matured forward-return labels at fixed horizons.
Sufficient support and dependence-aware train/evaluation separation; cost and fill labels for trading use.
methods.economicHypothesis: A smooth nonlinear return relationship could escape the bias of a linear fit while expressing where support is weak. Smoothness itself supplies no economic edge and covariance is model-dependent.

primarySources.title: Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, Chapter 2 (2006)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Linear-kernel GP posterior means can equal Bayesian linear/ridge regression; those are excluded as duplicates.
Different nonlinear kernels or length scales are configurations, not additional mechanisms.
GP uncertainty must not be reported as guaranteed financial coverage.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Only a small low-dimensional prototype is justified; overlapping multi-day labels sharply reduce effective sample size.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Use one predeclared nonlinear covariance on a small fixed causal feature map; compare predictive scores and then costed outcomes to the matching linear/kernel baselines.

methods.name: Multivariate Hawkes event-arrival forecasting
equations: Event log likelihood = sum_events log(lambda_event_type(t)) - sum_i integral lambda_i(t) dt.
methods.mechanismNovelty: Models causal excitation from individual event arrivals into future event intensities. Existing flow features and fill hazards are snapshot/history-summary formulas, not a fitted mutually exciting point-process likelihood.
requiredObservations: Sequence-accurate timestamped buy/sell events and possibly adds/cancels, with event classification and gap diagnostics.
Contemporaneous books and actual maker/taker costs for any executable profit test.
methods.economicHypothesis: Clustered aggressive order flow might help forecast near-term adverse price moves or avoid toxic entries. Arrival predictability need not produce a move larger than spot costs.

primarySources.title: Hawkes, Point Spectra of Some Mutually Exciting Point Processes (1971)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Changing flow lookbacks or log-hazard coefficients is excluded.
Exponential/power-law kernels, event marks and numbers of event types do not create separate families here.
A hybrid Hawkes plus queue-reactive model would overlap F04 and F05, not create an independent third mechanism by addition.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Daily OHLC destroys event-arrival order and cannot fit or validate event excitation.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: First audit prospective event-stream completeness; then fit event likelihood and assess unseen arrival prediction before execution economics.

methods.name: Queue-reactive Markov limit-order-book forecasting
equations: For price-direction hitting probability h, Lh=0 on interior states, h=1 at up-price boundary and h=0 at down-price boundary.
methods.mechanismNovelty: Infers event transition intensities conditional on actual queue states and solves a stochastic book evolution model. Existing depth/persistence features and heuristic maker hazard do not simulate a calibrated queue-state transition generator.
requiredObservations: Full sequence-consistent book additions, cancellations and trades with queue sizes and price changes.
Venue-specific matching/aggregation semantics, missing-message detection and execution costs.
methods.economicHypothesis: Book-state depletion probabilities could forecast adverse selection and attainable fills better than an aggregate imbalance. This primarily tests execution quality and very short-horizon price distribution.

primarySources.title: Huang, Lehalle and Rosenbaum, Simulating and Analyzing Order Book Data: The Queue-Reactive Model (2013/2014)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: A static imbalance threshold or assumed fill probability is excluded.
Changing depth levels or bucket discretizations is configuration, not new mathematics.
Unlike F04, the basic process is Markov in queue state rather than depending on the entire event-excitation history.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Requires a new book-event dataset; current daily bars are inadequate.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Estimate transition and held-out absorption probabilities on synchronized native books, including nonfills.

methods.name: Direct conditional quantile regression
methods.mechanismNovelty: Fits conditional quantiles directly through asymmetric absolute loss. Existing mean/ridge fits, Student-t location-scale estimates and empirical weighted quantiles do not optimize conditional regression quantiles.
requiredObservations: Causal features and matured net-return outcomes; enough tail observations at each declared quantile.
Consistent action, horizon and fill/cost conventions.
methods.economicHypothesis: Asymmetric downside may depend on features differently from mean return, so direct downside prediction could reject trades whose mean hides unfavorable tails. It need not increase average profit.

primarySources.title: Koenker and Bassett, Regression Quantiles (1978)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Changing a percentile in an existing empirical distribution is excluded.
Quantile levels and spline basis choices are configurations of the same estimator.
A forecast quantile is not a confidence bound for the mean and may lose calibration under regime changes.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: A central or moderate quantile prototype is possible; extreme-tail calibration lacks enough independent observations.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Compare predeclared pinball loss and empirical coverage against the existing empirical-distribution baseline.

methods.name: Dynamic conditional copula for joint asset dependence
methods.mechanismNovelty: Separates evolving cross-asset dependence, including asymmetric joint tails, from marginal return models. Inspected cross-asset Bayes predicts with observed regressors and experts but lacks a conditional copula joint density.
requiredObservations: Synchronized BTC/ETH returns and marginal predictive probability transforms.
Long enough history of joint stress events and a causal dependence-update schedule.
methods.economicHypothesis: Assets that appear diverse in ordinary periods may fail together in downturns; modeling tail dependence could improve allocation or abstention. It supplies joint risk information, not an automatic positive mean.

primarySources.title: Patton, Modelling Asymmetric Exchange Rate Dependence (2006)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Changing correlation windows or adding another observed BTC/ETH regressor is excluded.
Gaussian copula with fixed Gaussian margins collapses to ordinary multivariate Gaussian dependence; that special case is excluded.
Different copula names/parameters are not separately counted.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: A bivariate demonstration is possible; dependable dynamic tail estimation is not established by 720 daily bars.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Evaluate joint predictive scores and tail co-exceedance calibration before any allocation experiment.

methods.name: Causal temporal convolutional sequence learner
equations: Forecast r_(t+h) = g(h_t^(L)); all convolution indices are <=t.
methods.mechanismNovelty: Learns ordered lag interactions through a nonlinear causal sequence representation, unlike manually aggregated feature vectors supplied to ridge or shallow trees.
requiredObservations: Long causal input sequences and matured return/execution labels with gaps and publication lags tracked.
Much more independent data than the daily sample for meaningful generalization.
methods.economicHypothesis: An ordered sequence of pressure and recovery might carry information lost by snapshot aggregates. This remains an unproven crypto application; neural flexibility also increases fitting risk.

primarySources.title: Bai, Kolter and Koltun, An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling (2018)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Depth, width, dilation and activation changes are configurations.

For conservative counting, recurrent networks, attention networks and reservoir architecture alternatives are collapsed into this broad learned-sequence category rather than listed as many new systems.
A convolution with no nonlinear composition that reproduces an existing moving average is excluded.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Can be coded against 720 bars, but data would not support a meaningful learned-sequence search.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Obtain a sufficiently long independent sequence dataset, freeze architecture and compare against the same-feature simple learner.

methods.name: Conditional normalizing-flow density estimation
equations: z~p_0; y=T_theta(z;x), with T_theta invertible in z.
methods.mechanismNovelty: Learns a flexible density through invertible transformations and change-of-variables likelihood. Existing Student-t boosting limits conditional shape to location/scale, while empirical calibration reuses standardized residual shapes.
requiredObservations: Many matured causal outcome labels spanning conditional shapes and tails.
Held-out density and calibration checks with tail and support diagnostics.
methods.economicHypothesis: Conditional skew or multimodality beyond a fixed location-scale family might improve loss distribution estimates. Better likelihood alone does not establish profitable trade selection.

primarySources.title: Rezende and Mohamed, Variational Inference with Normalizing Flows (2015)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: An affine transform of one Student-t distribution is an existing location-scale special case and is excluded.
Flow layers, spline knots and base distributions do not count as independent mechanisms.
This source establishes flow-based inference; using a conditional flow for crypto executable outcomes is an application proposed here.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: The available daily sample is too small to justify a flexible conditional-density search.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Demonstrate conditional density misspecification on a larger fixed dataset before introducing flow complexity.

methods.name: Invariant causal prediction across independently defined environments
equations: For candidate predictor subset S, require Y^e = f_S(X_S^e)+epsilon^e with epsilon^e independent_of X_S^e and the same law across environments e.
Retain subsets not rejected by invariance tests; identifiable causal subset estimates use their intersection under the method assumptions.
methods.mechanismNovelty: Uses cross-environment invariance as an identifying restriction, rather than merely searching stable predictive correlations. Existing chronological tests and feature regimes do not implement invariant causal predictor selection.
requiredObservations: Observed environments with credible exogenous changes or intervention interpretation, predictor release timestamps and sufficient support in each.
A defensible structural assumption explaining which mechanism should remain invariant.
methods.economicHypothesis: Some predictive relationships may fail because they are regime-specific coincidences; an invariant mechanism could transfer better. Calendar partitions alone do not prove interventions or causality.

primarySources.title: Peters, Buhlmann and Meinshausen, Causal Inference Using Invariant Prediction (2015/2016)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Rebranding ordinary walk-forward validation as causal inference is excluded.
Arbitrary bull/bear period labels do not establish the required identification assumptions.
Changing accepted significance levels or chosen covariates is not a separate mathematical system.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Daily OHLC alone provides no defensible intervention/environment identification.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Define an externally grounded environment/data design and test assumptions before fitting an invariant predictor.

methods.name: Dynamic latent-factor forecasting from a broad panel
equations: Estimate the common factor span from past panel observations, then fit the forecast projection using matured labels.
methods.mechanismNovelty: Extracts a low-dimensional latent common process from a broad observed panel before forecasting. Inspected cross-asset models use a small hand-selected observed BTC/ETH feature vector rather than latent panel factors.
requiredObservations: Point-in-time broad asset or economic panel with historical constituent membership, missingness and release calendars.
Enough cross-sectional dimension and time coverage to separate common factors from idiosyncratic noise.
methods.economicHypothesis: Common liquidity or risk demand across many assets might summarize information that two-asset regressors miss. A macroeconomic factor forecasting method does not establish crypto return predictability.

primarySources.title: Stock and Watson, Macroeconomic Forecasting Using Diffusion Indexes (2002)
primarySources.supports: Established method, not profitability of the proposed crypto application.

nearestEquivalentsAndExclusions: Rotating or rescaling a fixed BTC/ETH feature vector is excluded.
Factor count, panel subsets and lag choices are configurations.
Factor extraction alone is not a trading strategy; the forecast and funded decision rule remain to be specified.

prototypeFeasibility.limitation: Two daily assets are inadequate for the intended broad latent-panel mechanism.
prototypeFeasibility.firstExperiment: Build the historically available broad panel; freeze factor extraction and compare incremental predictive value to observed-feature regression.

excludedOrCollapsed.reason: Implemented, including discounted Normal-inverse-gamma sufficient statistics and Student predictive uncertainty.
Implemented; changing bandwidth, distance or memory cannot create another mechanism.

excludedOrCollapsed.family: Shallow tree regime models and distributional boosting
excludedOrCollapsed.reason: CART partitions and Student-t natural-gradient boosting already implemented.
Implemented and researched; reset thresholds or changing reversion fits are not novel mechanisms.
Existing deterministic signal families and the 100-configuration screen cover these mechanisms.
Conservatively excluded because planner already computes competing log-linear fill and cancellation hazards; fitting richer baselines is a potential extension rather than a clean absent-family claim.
Conservatively excluded from count because existing EWMA variance is a closely related restricted recursion; a claim of substantial new mechanism requires a sharper model/estimation distinction.

excludedOrCollapsed.family: Linear Kalman filtering/particle filtering names alone
excludedOrCollapsed.reason: An inference algorithm alone does not establish a new economic/generative system; linear-Gaussian special cases overlap existing Bayesian linear estimation. No extra count without a distinct latent transition/observation model.

testedMechanismCountMeaning: Catalog mechanisms whose frozen historical replay by root was independently reviewed by this author; synthetic checks counted separately.
